title: Famous Door shifts, Tony Mitchell group and Bourbon Street bands
summary: Three bands play the Famous Door daily; Coquille moved from Nicky's Last Straws to the Tony Mitchell group, and he lists current bands on Bourbon Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, some band leaders, some band leaders let the trombone player go. Now, that was the case with The Last Straws when we went to Famous Goat some time back. They cut all three bands down. At the Famous Store right now, we have three bands, seven days a week, all year round, seven nights a week. First band comes on at 12, 15 to 5. We have the middle shift now. We used to have the night shift for many years. In fact, this is the first time in my life. I get home at 10.30 at night. Now, I'm used to getting home at 3 or 4 o'clock in the morning. First band comes on at 12, 15 to 5. Now, we come on at 5, 15 to 10. This third band comes on at 10, 15 to 3. Now, that's seven days a week. Now, we have a relief band that plays three nights a week there, relieving us on our day or night off, because we have to have a day or night off. We can only work six days or nights a week. And getting back to what I wanted to say, when they had cut the band down to five men, about a year ago, when I was with Nicky's Last Straws, we had six men there. I was there eight months with Nicky's Last Straws. They decided to cut down to five men. So they cut all three bands down to five men. And so they let the bass go. Well, I was home three weeks when they decided to let the trombone go. They missed the bass more than the trombone. Mm-hmm. So I went back to work. And that's when I went with the Tony Mitchell group. They called me back. Did they let Nicky go? No, no. Nick Gagliotti. No. They had let a bass horn player go with the Tony Mitchell group. Oh, I see. He was playing bass horn, I think. No, trombone. He was playing trombone with the Tony Mitchell group. And so they decided that they wanted the bass instead of the trombone. So that's when I joined the Tony Mitchell group. You see, Mitchell and Nicky were playing at the door. Two different bands.
And now they have different bands. Now there's three five piece bands there now.

You have Tony Mitchell. Tony Mitchell and the Famous Door Five. And you have Thomas Jefferson and his Creole Jazz Band. And at night you have, well, in the midst of a change right now, Jim LaRocca's going in at night now. Tommy Yedda was there at night, but he left. And Jim LaRocca is related to Nick LaRocca in some way. I don't know whether he's son or uncle, one or the other. He's son. And what about Jimmy Isle? Where is he? Jimmy Isle moved down to the Maison Bourbon. He has the early shift there. They work 11.30 to 4. Yeah. The second band comes on from 4 to 9. Who's got the second band now? Oh yeah, Howard Hollis Camus. Yes, I know him. Hollis Camus, who's an albino, plays clarinet, plays real fine clarinet and tenor sax. Hollis Camus, and he's a Cajun band, he calls it, I think. They're there from 5 to 9. And from 9 to 1 or 1.30, you have Lou Saino. Lou Saino is at the Maison Bourbon now. So they have three bands there. They have three bands at the Famous Door. And you have two bands at the Blue Angel. the Blue Angel. the Blue Angel. the Blue Angel. the Blue Angel.
